profile.name: Jangi
profile.tagline: A traditional Azerbaijani heroic military dance performed by men to evoke battle.
profile.insight: The name 'Jangi' derives from Persian roots meaning 'fighting,' and the dance serves as a historic, vigorous call-to-arms performed exclusively by men in the South Caucasus.
profile.profile: Jangi is a traditional Azerbaijani heroic military dance, historically rooted in the martial spirit of the region. Performed exclusively by men, it serves as a symbolic challenge to battle, reflecting the strength and courage of warriors. The dance is characterized by its vigorous, masculine movements and is traditionally set to music in a 2/4 time signature.
profile.profile_long: Jangi, known in Azerbaijani as Cəngi, is a national dance of Azerbaijan classified as a heroic military dance. The term itself is derived from Persian and translates to 'fighting,' reflecting the dance's historical function as a symbolic challenge to battle. It is considered a very ancient tradition, serving as a reminder of the historical struggles of strong men and performed in their honor. In the context of the South Caucasus, it is distinctly categorized as a war dance, designed to evoke the courage and martial spirit of the performers. Performance of the dance is restricted to men, typically occurring during holidays or at concerts. The musical foundation of the dance is based on the shur mode, played in a 2/4 time signature. Dancers wear traditional Azerbaijani costumes, which consist of a colorful long jacket, trousers, and a pair of boots. Because the sources provide limited information regarding specific choreography, technical footwork, or the exact historical timeline of its development, many aspects of the dance's physical execution remain undocumented in the current literature.

sections.costume_and_setting: Dancers wear traditional Azerbaijani costumes, which include a colorful long jacket, trousers, and a pair of boots. It is performed during holidays or at concerts.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: Jangi functions as a heroic military dance, serving as a symbolic challenge to battle and a tribute to the strength of men.
